title: What does a management consulting firm actually do?
description: A plain-English explanation of what consulting firms sell, who hires them, what a project looks like and why companies pay for outside advice.
hook: If you are thinking about consulting but are not quite sure what consultants actually do, you are in good company. The job is famously hard to explain at family dinners. Here is the simple version: what consulting firms sell, who buys it, and what a project really looks like from the inside.
body:
The short answer

Consulting firms help organisations solve problems they cannot, or would rather not, solve alone. A company hires a team of consultants for a set period, usually a few weeks to a few months, to answer a specific question or deliver a specific change, and pays for that team's time and expertise.

Why would a company pay for outside help?

  • Extra hands for a big question. Executives are busy running the business. A focused team can spend eight weeks on one problem full time.
  • Experience from elsewhere. Consultants have often seen the same problem at other companies and industries, so they know what tends to work.
  • An outside view. A neutral team can say things insiders find hard to say, and can help a leadership team agree on a decision.
  • Specialist skills. Pricing, supply chains, technology, mergers and data analysis all need expertise a company may not keep in-house.

What kinds of questions do clients bring?

Almost exactly the questions you practise in case interviews: why are profits falling, should we enter this market, should we buy this company, how do we cut costs by 15%, how should we price a new product, how do we make this hospital or government service work better. That is not a coincidence. Case interviews are designed to look like the work.

Who are the clients?

Large companies in every industry, private equity funds, governments and public bodies, and non-profits. The person who hires the consultants is usually a senior executive, and the team works closely with that executive's own staff.

What does a project look like?

  1. Scoping. Agree the question, the deadline and what success looks like.
  2. Hypotheses and a work plan. Make early guesses at the answer and plan the analysis to test them.
  3. Analysis. Gather data, interview people inside and outside the company, build models, visit sites.
  4. Synthesis. Turn the findings into a clear story and recommendation, usually as a slide deck.
  5. Decision and, often, implementation. Present to leadership; many projects continue into helping the client make the change happen.

Is it all strategy?

No. Strategy work (what should we do?) is the best-known part, but a large share of consulting is operations, technology and implementation (how do we do it, and do it well?). This guide explains the different types.

Sources

  • Hacking the Case Interview: What is management consulting?

Checked November 2026.

What the client actually buys

Imagine a retailer asking whether to open 40 smaller shops. Management can produce its own opinions, but it may lack time to assess 40 locations, model footfall, interview customers and compare the economics with existing stores. A consulting team can bring a structured process and additional analytical capacity, then help management make a decision.

A typical engagement might begin with two weeks of clarifying the question and collecting facts, move into several weeks of customer research and financial modelling, and finish with options and a recommendation. The deliverable is not simply a slide deck. It might include an investment decision, an operating plan, a pricing test or an implementation roadmap. The client still owns the final decision.

This is why case interviews focus on problem definition, analysis, synthesis and communication. You are being asked to demonstrate a miniature version of consulting work. Ask yourself after every practice case: if the client's chief executive had five minutes, could they understand the decision, supporting numbers and principal uncertainty?
